scope: Actual TrainerFrame typed movement IPC integration; synthetic rejection and retained-receipt replay only.
entrypoint: TypedMovementIntegrationTests, called from main before the existing command checks

run.compiler_flags: MSVC x64, /std:c++17 /O2 /W4 /MT /EHsc; no compiler warnings in the captured log

verified: Command 1466 passes through the production TrainerFrame dispatcher, not a direct call to movement_tx::Execute.

The 128-byte request at offset 1024 is preserved. The 192-byte response at offset 1152 has the matching shared and binary request sequence, schema, client ID, operation ID, nonce and current tick. A tail canary checks the response extent; the snapshot seqlock finishes even.
An already acknowledged shared request sequence does not execute again or replace the response.
New packets with commandIssuedAt zero, age 8000 ms, or a future timestamp reject Expired without reserving a receipt.
Every one of the eight generic scalar arguments rejects when 1.0, NaN or positive infinity; no new typed mutation receipt is reserved.
Zero or expired host heartbeat rejects a new packet as HostExpired without a new receipt.
A synthetically faulted ActorLifetime observer rejects a fresh valid Acquire as ObserverFault and stores an immutable rejection receipt.
Identical duplicates replay the retained rejection despite expired command, expired host or malformed scalar arguments; the original receipt is unchanged.
An explicitly seeded prior Applied receipt is replayed unchanged despite the same pre-rejections. This checks replay only and does not simulate a successful new native mutation or lease.
The same operation ID with changed desired bits rejects RequestIdConflict and leaves its retained receipt unchanged.
Wrong schema and stale bridge nonce reject UnsupportedSchema and StaleBridge.
Snapshot slots 466..471 publish supported, valid schema 1 diagnostics; Fault publishes zero generation, exact 32-bit nonce halves and observer status 2.
No new lease, Actor/status field change or constructor/destructor hook-slot change occurs; the fixture restores private journal, observer and shared state before the existing tests.
limits: The test uses synthetic memory, a faulted observer and a fixed nonce. It does not install lifetime hooks, inject into a process or execute game functions.
Successful fresh acquire/reapply/release writes and real constructor/destructor observations are outside this integration fixture and belong to their dedicated synthetic suites.
The response sequence check observes the completed TrainerFrame call; it does not independently prove interprocess memory ordering under concurrent access.
No full build or other test suite was run for this assignment.
